meta.notes: The formulas a character sheet computes, each citing where it is printed: the ability modifier, Proficiency Bonus, saving throws, ability and skill checks (with Expertise), Passive Perception, Initiative and the Initiative score, base AC, spell save DC and attack modifier, Hit Points at level 1 and per level (fixed and rolled), carrying capacity and drag/lift/push, the Concentration DC, weapon and Unarmed Strike attack and damage, the multiclass spellcaster level, and the jumps. Formulas that need a parameter (which ability or skill), a proficiency state, the class's Hit Die, the character's size, or an input at play (damage, a roll) carry a computeNote with the tree they would have under a proposed node. dependsOn names ability:<a>, level, class, class-level:<id>, size, proficiency:<category>, expertise:<category>, effects:<target>, advantage:<target>, or another derivation's id. Armor AC formulas are equipment.json's and features'.

derivations.name: Ability Modifier
derivations.display: floor((score − 10) ÷ 2), as on the Ability Modifiers table
derivations.computeNote: The vocabulary has no parameter for 'the ability (or skill) in question', and no node for a proficiency state, so one tree cannot cover every ability. Per ability a: {floorDiv: {sum: [abilityScore a, constant −10]}, by 2}, which is what the abilityMod node computes. The app evaluates abilityMod; core.json's abilityModifiers holds the printed table to test it against.

source.section: Playing the Game > The Six Abilities > Ability Modifiers

derivations.note: The SRD prints a table (p.6), not a formula, and says to round down (p.5). The formula reproduces every row of the table for scores 1 to 30; checked by the build script.

derivations.name: Proficiency Bonus
derivations.display: +2 at character levels 1–4, +3 at 5–8, +4 at 9–12, +5 at 13–16, +6 at 17–20

source.section: Character Creation > Level Advancement

derivations.note: By total character level, not a class's level (Multiclassing > Proficiency Bonus, p.25).

derivations.name: Saving Throw
derivations.display: ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus if you have proficiency in that kind of save
derivations.computeNote: The vocabulary has no parameter for 'the ability (or skill) in question', and no node for a proficiency state, so one tree cannot cover every ability. Per ability a: {sum: [abilityMod a, {product: [proficiencyBonus, proficiencyMultiplier save a]}]} plus effects on save:a and save:all, where proficiencyMultiplier is a proposed node (0 or 1 here).

source.section: Character Creation > Step 5: Character Creation Details > Fill In Numbers

derivations.note: Saving Throws (p.7) says the same: 'You add your Proficiency Bonus to your saving throw if you have proficiency in that kind of save.'

derivations.name: Ability Check
derivations.display: ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus when a skill or tool proficiency you have is relevant
derivations.computeNote: The vocabulary has no parameter for 'the ability (or skill) in question', and no node for a proficiency state, so one tree cannot cover every ability. Per ability a, with the relevant proficiency p: {sum: [abilityMod a, {product: [proficiencyBonus, proficiencyMultiplier p]}]} plus effects on check:a and check:all. The Proficiency Bonus is added once even if two proficiencies apply (The Bonus Doesn’t Stack, p.8); proficiency in both the skill and the tool also gives Advantage (Equipment Proficiencies, p.9).

source.section: Playing the Game > D20 Tests > Ability Checks

derivations.name: Skill Check
derivations.display: the skill’s ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus if proficient, doubled with Expertise
derivations.computeNote: The vocabulary has no parameter for 'the ability (or skill) in question', and no node for a proficiency state, so one tree cannot cover every ability. Per skill s with ability a (skills.json): {sum: [abilityMod a, {product: [proficiencyBonus, proficiencyMultiplier skill s]}]} plus effects on skill:s, check:a and check:all; proficiencyMultiplier is 0 without proficiency, 1 proficient, 2 with Expertise. Expertise doubles the bonus 'unless the bonus is doubled by another feature' (Rules Glossary, Expertise, p.182), and a Proficiency Bonus can be multiplied only once (p.8).

source.section: Character Creation > Step 5: Character Creation Details > Fill In Numbers

derivations.note: Fill In Numbers > Skills (p.22) gives modifier + Proficiency Bonus; the Expertise doubling is the Rules Glossary's Expertise (p.182).

derivations.name: Passive Perception
derivations.display: 10 + Wisdom (Perception) check bonus; +5 with Advantage, −5 with Disadvantage on such checks
derivations.computeNote: The tree needs the Wisdom (Perception) check total and whether those checks have Advantage or Disadvantage, which the vocabulary has no node for: {sum: [constant 10, derivation skill-check(perception), advantageAdjust(+5/−5)]}. The app takes the Perception total and adds 5 or subtracts 5 when every Wisdom (Perception) check has Advantage or Disadvantage. effects on passive:perception also apply.

source.section: Rules Glossary > Passive Perception

derivations.note: Fill In Numbers (p.22) prints 'Passive Perception = 10 + Wisdom (Perception) check modifier'; the glossary adds the ±5.

derivations.name: Initiative
derivations.display: Dexterity modifier (Initiative is a Dexterity check)

source.section: Character Creation > Step 5: Character Creation Details > Fill In Numbers

derivations.note: Effects on initiative add to it. Whether effects on Dexterity checks also add is open: see core.json ambiguity initiative-includes-dexterity-check-bonuses.

derivations.name: Initiative Score
derivations.display: 10 + Dexterity modifier; +5 with Advantage on Initiative rolls, −5 with Disadvantage

source.section: Rules Glossary > Initiative

derivations.note: Used when the GM has combatants use Initiative scores instead of rolling. The ±5 for Advantage or Disadvantage is applied by the app; the vocabulary has no node for it.

derivations.name: Base AC
derivations.display: 10 + Dexterity modifier

source.section: Playing the Game > D20 Tests > Attack Rolls > Armor Class

derivations.note: 'Base AC = 10 + the creature’s Dexterity modifier' (p.7); also Rules Glossary, Armor Class (p.177) and Fill In Numbers (p.22: 'Without armor or a shield'). Another base AC calculation replaces it; only one applies.

derivations.name: Spell Save DC
derivations.display: 8 + your spellcasting ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus

source.section: Spells > Casting Spells > Effects > Saving Throws

derivations.note: Also Fill In Numbers (p.23). The spellcasting ability is the one of the feature that gives the spell; multiclassed, the ability of the class the spell is prepared for (p.25).

derivations.name: Spell Attack Modifier
derivations.display: your spellcasting ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus

source.section: Spells > Casting Spells > Effects > Attack Rolls

derivations.note: Called 'Spell attack bonus' in Fill In Numbers (p.23).

derivations.name: Hit Points at Level 1
derivations.display: Barbarian 12, Fighter, Paladin or Ranger 10, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Monk, Rogue or Warlock 8, Sorcerer or Wizard 6; + Con. modifier
derivations.computeNote: The value depends on the first class, which a tree cannot read: the vocabulary has no node for a class's Hit Point Die. With a proposed hitDie node: {sum: [hitDie first-class, abilityMod con]} (each printed value is the class's Hit Die size, classes.json hitDie). Multiclassed, the level 1 Hit Points come only from the class taken at character level 1 (p.25).

source.section: Character Creation > Step 5: Character Creation Details > Fill In Numbers

derivations.name: Hit Points per Level (Fixed)
derivations.display: Barbarian 7, Fighter, Paladin or Ranger 6, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Monk, Rogue or Warlock 5, Sorcerer or Wizard 4; + Con. modifier
derivations.computeNote: Per level gained, by the class the level is taken in; the vocabulary has no node for a class's Hit Point Die. Each printed value is half the class's Hit Die + 1, so with a proposed hitDie node: {sum: [floorDiv(hitDie class, 2), constant 1, abilityMod con]}. Whether 'minimum of 1' applies to this option is open: see ambiguity fixed-hit-points-minimum. A change to the Constitution modifier changes every level's share (Gaining a Level, step 5).

source.section: Character Creation > Level Advancement > Gaining a Level

derivations.name: Hit Points per Level (Rolled)
derivations.display: roll the class’s Hit Die + Con. modifier (minimum of 1)
derivations.computeNote: The roll is stored on the character for each level; the vocabulary has no node for a stored roll. With a proposed input node: {max: [constant 1, {sum: [input roll, abilityMod con]}]}.

source.section: Character Creation > Level Advancement > Gaining a Level

derivations.name: Carrying Capacity
derivations.display: Strength score × 15 lb. (Small or Medium); Tiny × 7.5, Large × 30, Huge × 60, Gargantuan × 120
derivations.computeNote: The multiplier depends on the character's size, which a tree cannot read. The app multiplies the Strength score by core.json sizes[size].carryingMultiplier; with a proposed sizeValue node: {product: [abilityScore str, sizeValue carryingMultiplier]}.

source.section: Rules Glossary > Carrying Capacity

derivations.name: Drag, Lift, or Push
derivations.display: Strength score × 30 lb. (Small or Medium); Tiny × 15, Large × 60, Huge × 120, Gargantuan × 240
derivations.computeNote: As carrying-capacity, from the table's Drag/Lift/Push column, which core.json's sizes record in their notes. While dragging, lifting, or pushing more than you can carry, your Speed can be no more than 5 feet.

source.section: Rules Glossary > Carrying Capacity

derivations.name: Concentration Save DC
derivations.display: 10 or half the damage taken (round down), whichever is higher, up to a maximum of 30
derivations.computeNote: The damage taken is an input at the moment of play, which the vocabulary has no node for. With a proposed input node: {min: [constant 30, {max: [constant 10, floorDiv(input damage, 2)]}]}.

source.section: Rules Glossary > Concentration

derivations.name: Melee Attack Bonus
derivations.display: Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus

source.section: Character Creation > Step 5: Character Creation Details > Fill In Numbers

derivations.note: For a weapon with which you have proficiency, 'unless a weapon’s property says otherwise' (Finesse: Strength or Dexterity, p.89). Without proficiency the Proficiency Bonus is not added (p.9); never with an improvised weapon (p.183).

derivations.name: Ranged Attack Bonus
derivations.display: Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus

source.section: Character Creation > Step 5: Character Creation Details > Fill In Numbers

derivations.note: For a weapon with which you have proficiency, 'unless a weapon’s property says otherwise' (a Thrown melee weapon uses its melee ability, p.90). Without proficiency the Proficiency Bonus is not added (p.9).

derivations.name: Weapon Damage Modifier
derivations.display: the same ability modifier used for the attack roll
derivations.computeNote: It is whichever ability modifier the attack used (Strength, Dexterity, or a choice under Finesse), which a tree cannot pick. The app reuses the attack's abilityMod node. Exception: the Light property's Bonus Action attack adds it only if it is negative (p.89); it is not added to fixed damage that doesn't use a roll (p.16).

source.section: Playing the Game > Combat > Damage and Healing > Damage Rolls

derivations.name: Unarmed Strike Attack Bonus
derivations.display: Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus

source.section: Rules Glossary > Unarmed Strike

derivations.name: Unarmed Strike Damage
derivations.display: 1 + Strength modifier (Bludgeoning)

source.section: Rules Glossary > Unarmed Strike

derivations.note: A penalty can bring damage to 0 but not below (Damage Rolls, p.16).

derivations.name: Grapple and Shove DC
derivations.display: 8 + Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus

source.section: Rules Glossary > Unarmed Strike

derivations.note: The DC for the Grapple option's save and any escape attempts, and for the Shove option's save.

derivations.name: Multiclass Spellcaster Level
derivations.display: all your levels in Bard, Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer and Wizard + half your levels (round up) in Paladin and Ranger

source.section: Character Creation > Multiclassing > Class Features > Spellcasting

derivations.note: Used only once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class; the result is looked up in spellcasting.json's multiclassSlots. Round up is written as floor((levels + 1) ÷ 2), since the vocabulary has only floorDiv; a class you don't have counts 0. Warlock levels don't count (Pact Magic stays apart).

derivations.name: Long Jump
derivations.display: up to your Strength score in feet with a 10-foot run-up; half that standing

source.section: Rules Glossary > Long Jump

derivations.note: The running distance; the standing jump is half (round down, p.5), which the app halves.

derivations.name: High Jump
derivations.display: 3 + Strength modifier feet (minimum of 0) with a 10-foot run-up; half that standing

source.section: Rules Glossary > High Jump

derivations.note: The running height; the standing jump is half (round down, p.5), which the app halves.

ambiguities.question: Does Gaining a Level's 'minimum of 1' apply when you take the fixed Hit Points value instead of rolling?

readings.text: Yes: 'Instead of rolling' replaces only the roll, so the total added is still at least 1 (a Sorcerer or Wizard with a Constitution modifier of −4 or less would otherwise gain 0 or fewer).
No: the minimum is written into the rolling sentence; the fixed value is the table's number plus the Con. modifier, whatever it comes to.

source.section: Character Creation > Level Advancement > Gaining a Level

ruling.note: The minimum of 1 applies to the fixed value too: 'instead of rolling' replaces only the roll.
